(CNN) -- A 4-year-old Ohio girl who vanished more than three weeks ago was found alive and in good condition, halfway across the country in southern California, authorities said. Haylee Donathan was found with her mother and her mother's boyfriend, fugitive sex offender Robbie Potter. Haylee Donathan, her mother Candace Watson and Robbie Potter were discovered hiding for the past week at The Morning Star Ranch, a retreat in Valley Center, near San Diego, said Peter Elliott, United States Marshal for the Northern District of Ohio. Potter is a registered sex offender, officials said. He was being sought by the U.S. Marshal's Service. Late Tuesday Haylee was in the custody of a children's protective services agency in the San Diego County area, Elliott said. She was doing well but may have chicken pox, he added. "We understand she is healthy and happy and I believe, waiting to come back to her grandmother here," he said.  Watch authorities announce their find » . The journey west took them more than two thousand miles from Mansfield, the north-Central Ohio city where the girl and her mother live. "I am very happy that my granddaughter's coming home," said Mary Watson, Haylee's grandmother. "And I just want to thank all of you from the bottom of my heart." Watson, 24, and Potter, 27, were arrested without incident and held by the San Diego County Sheriff's Department. When asked their reaction, Elliott said, "I believe a little shocked that we were able to find them." Potter and Watson were still using the same vehicle, a 1980s blue Chevrolet pickup truck they drove from Ohio, Elliott said. Watson's hair was a bit darker and Potter also changed his appearance slightly. Authorities had feared Haylee was endangered. Potter, a sex offender, had escaped a half-way house on May 28, the day the girl and her mother fell out of sight. Countless tips came in while they were missing but one in particular led to the breakthrough on Tuesday, Elliott said without elaborating. But a tip from members of the ranch could have lead to the raid and arrest, a ranchmember told CNN. Kevin Carlin, a member of the ranch in the neighborhood of Valley Center, told CNN in a telephone interview that ranch members became suspicious when a former ranch guest saw billboards urging help in finding Haylee and the two adults. Elliott also praised intense national news coverage from programs such as HLN's Nancy Grace and Issues with Jane Velez-Mitchell, as well as local media and Clear Channel, which put up missing child billboards across the country. When she is returned to Ohio, Haylee will be placed in the custody of her grandmother, Elliott said. The U.S. Marshals Northern Ohio Violent Fugitive Task Force had offered a $10,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of 27-year-old Potter. Potter was wanted on a state warrant for parole violation and a federal warrant for probation violation. He is a convicted tier three sex offender, according to the U.S. Marshals Service, a unit of the Justice Department. While on the run, Potter and Watson were reportedly seen on surveillance video on May 31 at a Wal-Mart Store in Marion, Ohio, 40 miles from Mansfield. Haylee was not on that video. Adding to concerns, Watson's roommate, Samantha Covert, said last week in an interview on Nancy Grace that she saw the little girl in bed with her mother and Potter the morning they disappeared. Covert said Watson carried a basket of clothing, pillows and blankets. Watson will likely face state charges, including harboring a fugitive, according to Elliott. In addition to other charges, he said Potter may be prosecuted under the Adam Walsh Child Protection and Safety Act, a federal sex offender registration and self-reporting law that carries a multi-year felony sentence if violated. On its Web site, the Morning Star Ranch describes itself as "a community of growers of organic, pesticide-free avocados, grapefruit, persimmons, nuts, and other produce." Elliot said he believed it is a rehab facility and also called it a Christian retreat.

# Missing Mansfield Girl Found at California Ranch After Cross-Country Search

**Investigation spanned more than 2,000 miles before tip led authorities to Christian retreat near San Diego**

---

MANSFIELD, Ohio — A 14-year-old girl who vanished from her Mansfield home nearly three months ago has been found safe at a Christian retreat ranch outside San Diego, California, bringing a dramatic close to a multi-state investigation that authorities say was cracked open by a viewer who recognized her face from a news broadcast.

The girl, whose name is being withheld because she is a minor, was located last week at a residential facility in the rural hills of eastern San Diego County, more than 2,000 miles from the neighborhood where she was last seen. Authorities have taken an adult into custody in connection with her disappearance, and prosecutors in both Ohio and California are now weighing charges.

## A Disappearance That Puzzled Investigators

The case began in the early autumn, when the teenager was reported missing by her family after she failed to return home. Mansfield police initially classified the case as a possible runaway, but detectives grew increasingly concerned as days stretched into weeks with no confirmed sightings and no activity on the girl's known accounts.

"Early on, we had very little to work with," said a detective with the Mansfield Division of Police who worked the case. "There were no eyewitnesses to an abduction, no ransom demand, nothing that pointed us clearly in one direction. What we did have was a young girl who was simply gone."

Investigators pursued digital leads, subpoenaing phone records and social media accounts, but the trail repeatedly went cold. Detectives suspected early on that the girl had not left entirely of her own accord — or at least that an adult had helped facilitate and conceal her movement across state lines, a circumstance that can elevate a missing-persons case into a federal matter.

The FBI's local resident agency was brought in to assist, given the possibility that the girl had been transported across state lines. The National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) also joined the effort, distributing the girl's photograph and physical description through its national network.

## The Role of Media Coverage

With the investigation stalling, the girl's family made a public plea, appearing before television cameras and sharing photographs across local and regional news outlets. That decision, authorities now say, proved decisive.

"Media coverage in a case like this is not a footnote — it is often the single most powerful tool we have," a police spokesperson said at a press conference following the recovery. "We can knock on a thousand doors, but a photograph on the evening news reaches a million people at once. Someone out there always knows something."

For weeks, the story circulated across Ohio broadcasts and online, then spread as the search widened. The girl's image was picked up by outlets in other states and shared thousands of times on social media platforms.

The break finally came from an unlikely source. A person affiliated with — or living near — the California ranch reportedly saw a news segment or online post about the missing Ohio teen and recognized her as a young resident who had recently arrived at the facility. That individual contacted a tip line.

"It was one tip," the detective said. "One person who did the right thing. That's what closed the distance between Ohio and California."

## The Ranch Near San Diego

The facility where the girl was found is described as a faith-based retreat and ranch that markets itself as a place of spiritual renewal and youth ministry. Set on a sprawling property in the backcountry east of San Diego, the ranch had reportedly taken the girl in.

Investigators are examining how the girl came to be at the facility, who transported her there, and whether staff or leadership were aware that she was a missing child reported to law enforcement. Authorities have stressed that the investigation into the ranch's role is ongoing and that no determination has yet been made about the broader institution's knowledge or conduct.

When San Diego County sheriff's deputies, acting on the tip and in coordination with Ohio investigators and the FBI, arrived at the property, they located the girl and confirmed her identity. She was reported to be physically unharmed.

"She's safe. That's the headline that matters most today," a sheriff's department official said. "Everything else — the charges, the accountability — that process now begins. But a family that has been living a nightmare finally has their daughter back."

## An Arrest and the Legal Aftermath

Authorities confirmed that an adult has been arrested in connection with the girl's disappearance and transport. The suspect faces potential charges that could include interference with custody, contributing to the delinquency or unruliness of a minor, and, depending on the findings, more serious felony counts related to the transport of a minor across state lines.

Because the girl was moved from Ohio to California, the case carries federal dimensions. Federal prosecutors may pursue charges under statutes governing the interstate transport of minors, while state prosecutors in Ohio and California evaluate their own potential counts.

"When a child is taken across multiple state lines, you can end up with overlapping jurisdictions," a former prosecutor not involved in the case explained. "You'll often see coordination between local district attorneys, the state attorney general's offices, and the U.S. Attorney's Office to determine where the strongest case can be brought and who prosecutes first."

Legal experts note that the involvement of a religious institution adds complexity. Investigators will need to establish what representations were made about the girl, whether adults at the facility conducted any verification of her identity or age, and whether anyone knowingly harbored a child they understood to be missing.

The girl's family, through a representative, expressed gratitude to law enforcement, the media, and the anonymous tipster.

"We never stopped believing she would come home," the family said in a brief statement. "To the person who made that call — you gave us back our child. There are no words for that kind of gift."

## The Journey Home

The teenager was placed in the care of child protective services in California pending arrangements for her return to Ohio, a standard procedure that also allows for medical evaluation and forensic interviews conducted by specialists trained to work with recovered children.

Advocates say the aftermath of recovery is often as delicate as the search itself.

"Finding a child is the beginning, not the end," said a spokesperson for a child-advocacy organization familiar with such cases. "There is a long road of reunification, counseling, and healing ahead.
